title: The PR: evidence, judge, Byte and the ready gate
bridge: Nova's PR is like a PR you write from the team template, opened as a draft until CI is green. Except: every claim points to proof in an evidence pack, and a judge checks the words first. People are pinged only when a gate says the PR is clean.
intro: This lesson turns a finished build into a PR people can trust. Nova renders the body from the pr-story template, a PR judge checks every claim, and Byte reviews the draft. A ready gate marks the PR ready only when nothing is left open. Then exactly one person who is not the requester approves.

picture.caption: From the evidence pack to a ready PR. Nobody is pinged while the PR is a draft.

steps.text: collects before and after runs, videos, the checks table, the receipt and the trace link
render() writes the body; the judge checks each claim against the diff and the evidence
opens the PR as a draft through the broker and asks Byte to review
posts findings; Nova fixes or answers each important one
CI green, QA passed, judges clean, nothing important open: gh pr ready
requests the team by area; the Jira ticket goes back to the requester
exactly one approval, from someone who is not the requester

sections.h: Start from what a reviewer opens
p: Picture a reviewer from the BE guild opening a Nova PR about a React table. They do not know the area. They read the top of the body, look at the checks table, open one video, and decide where to start.

Everything on that page comes from the evidence pack: the proof a run collected. It holds the before and after test runs, a short video per UI check and the checks table from checks.json. It also holds the self-review receipt, the trace link and the harness suggestions. Files live in .nova/ on the branch and in S3.
The body uses the pr-story template from G8, the same headings on every PR. G8 replaces fcp's 4-section .github/pull_request_template.md with it, together with the guilds. One template, not two.
This lesson follows the run: render the body, judge it, open a draft, let Byte review, then the ready gate.

sections.h: The PR body, part 1: what, why and the checks
p: render() is a pure function: evidence in, markdown out. Part 1 writes the top of the body. Above the fold, the part a reviewer sees without scrolling, stays under about 300 words. Long output is linked, never pasted.
The checks table has one row per QA check from qa_results.json: what the user sees, the result, the proof. Under it, links to the failing-before and passing-after runs.
sections.because: The same headings on every PR mean anyone, from any team, knows where to look for proof.

notes.text: Evidence is everything the run collected, loaded from .nova/ and S3: plan, checks, QA results, receipt, links.
A small helper: a markdown list, or "- None." when the list is empty, so a heading is never left bare.
Pure: it reads the evidence and returns a string. A fixture file is enough to test it.
One table row per QA check, for example | QA-1: <user sees> | pass | <video link> |.
The pr-story headings start here. What changes is one short paragraph for a reader from another team.
Why names the ticket and the root cause with its file and line, so a reviewer can jump there.
The table header. Every row links to proof, never to a claim.
The before run (lesson g4-3) and the after run. Seeing the test fail first is the strongest proof.

sections.h: The PR body, part 2: limits, risk and Requested-by
p: Part 2 says what was not checked and why, from the skips in checks.json. Then risk and rollback and where to look first. Last, a folded details block: the receipt, the trace, the harness suggestions, cost and time.

Media appear only where the QA plan asked. That is a video of 30 seconds or less for a flow, or screenshots at 760 and 1440 for layout. API and CLI output stays text. Seed data only, never pictures of code or logs.
GitHub has no API for PR attachments. So media is linked from the evidence bucket through a small authenticated viewer. How it is served is a decision with DevOps; the bucket is never public.
sections.because: The last line names the requester, because the independent-approval check reads it to refuse that person's approval.

notes.text: Every skip from checks.json with its reason. A reviewer can disagree with a choice only if they can see it.
Risk and its reason come from the plan. Rollback is always a revert; Watch says what to look at after merge.
A few paths with one line each: where the important change is, so review starts in the right place.
A folded block. Useful for the curious, out of the way for everyone else.
The receipt line from lesson g4-4: found, fixed, left, because. Byte reads the same receipt.
Cost and minutes are shown to learn from. Nothing stops a run because of them.
Kept as in fcp's template, so add-jira-links.yml finds the Jira link and leaves the body alone.
The GitHub login from config/people.yaml. G0's independent-approval check reads this line.

callout.text: The Requested-by line is written by the harness from the run's requester, never typed by the model. Exactly one approval counts, and never the requester's.

sections.h: The PR judge reads like the other team
p: Agents tend to overclaim: "all edge cases handled". The PR judge reads the description first, as a reviewer would on GitHub. Then it checks each claim against the diff and the evidence. A claim with no proof is flagged.

It runs in its own query() session on Sonnet 5.5 at medium, with structured output from a zod schema. Its tools are Read, Grep and Glob. No Bash, because git diff --output= writes files; the harness writes the diff to a file first, as in lesson g4-4.

Its input is the description, the diff and the evidence pack. Never the transcript. Nova rewrites the description and the judge reads it again. An item that comes back twice stays as a note for the reviewer instead of another round.
sections.because: A clear, true description is what lets anyone review any area, so we check it before a person spends time on it.

code.text:
<!-- ai-agents/harness/prompts/pr-judge.md: the PR judge. Input: the PR description, `git diff origin/main...HEAD`, the evidence pack. -->
You are a reviewer from the other team. You did not write this change and you don't know this area well.
Read the PR description first, the way you would on GitHub. Then check it against the diff and the evidence.

For every claim in the description, ask:
- Is it in the diff? ("Adds a loading state" → find the loading state.)
- Is there proof? A check marked pass needs a test run, a video or a transcript in the evidence pack.
- Would I understand it without opening the Jira ticket?

Also check the shape: What changes, Why, How it was checked, What was not checked and why, Risk and rollback,
Where to look first, then the folded receipt, References and the Requested-by line. Above the fold stays under
about 300 words. No pasted logs. Pictures and videos only for checks that asked for them, each labelled.

Flag only what would confuse or mislead a reviewer. A clear, true description with nothing to flag is a good result.
Return {"ready": bool, "items": [{"sentence", "problem": "unclear|not_in_diff|no_proof|missing|too_long", "suggestion"}]}.

notes.text: The file's header: the three inputs. git diff origin/main...HEAD is the change since the branch left main.
The point of view: someone who does not know the area. Clarity is judged from there.
Claim one: find it in the diff. "Adds a loading state" means a loading state must be there.
Claim two: a check marked pass needs a test run, a video or a transcript in the evidence pack.
Claim three: the description stands on its own.
The pr-story headings in order, the folded receipt, References and the Requested-by line.
Guidance, not a hunt: a clean description with nothing to flag is a good result.
The answer shape. The zod schema in the harness matches it: ready, and items with a problem and a rewrite.

sections.h: Open a draft and ask Byte
p: A draft PR is a PR GitHub marks as not ready for review. Reviewers are not asked and the ruleset does not count it as ready. Nova opens its PR as a draft, so people are not pinged until it is clean.

Every call goes through the broker, which holds the GitHub token and an allow-list of commands. Nova's allow-list gets pr edit and pr ready. Byte stays independent of Nova's self-review; that is why it is worth having.

For each important Byte finding, Nova fixes it and replies "Fixed in <sha>", or replies with its reason. Byte's findings get fingerprints like self-review findings (lesson g4-4). One that returns after a fix goes to the requester in Slack.
sections.because: Byte reviews while the PR is a draft, so its findings are handled before any person reads the PR.

code.file: Nova's broker calls for the draft (sketch)
code.text:
# Nova's GitHub calls for the draft (a sketch built from G4-26's steps). Each one runs through the broker.
gh pr create --draft --title "[FE] RH-1234: Empty projects table shows a No projects yet card" \
  --body-file .nova/pr.md --head nova/RH-1234-empty-projects-card
gh pr edit 2512 --add-reviewer RhinoHealth/byte              # ask Byte for a review
gh api repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/pulls/2512/comments              # read Byte's inline comments (Byte's app only)
gh api repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/pulls/2512/comments/9001/replies -f body="Fixed in 3f2c1ab"
# Nits are counted, not fixed. A finding that returns after a fix goes to the requester in Slack.
# Never: gh run rerun, gh workflow run. Each push re-runs CI by itself.

notes.text: A draft PR. The title follows fcp's style: [FE] RH-1234: what changes for the user.
The body render() wrote. The head branch starts with nova/, as the broker's git proxy requires.
Requesting the byte team is how Byte is asked to review.
Read Byte's inline comments through the broker. Only comments from Byte's app are acted on.
Reply in the thread. Check the broker's allow-list covers this call.
Nova never re-runs or dispatches workflows. A push triggers CI on its own.

callout.text: The G4-26 ticket replies to Byte with gh api .../comments/<id>/replies, but that call is not on the broker's allow-list. Add it to Nova's allow-list in the same PR, next to pr edit and pr ready. Otherwise the broker refuses every reply.

sections.h: Let Byte see drafts: a change a person makes
p: Today Byte never sees a Nova draft. fcp's byte-review.yml reviews pull_request events only when draft is false, and its comment path skips bots. So one condition must change.
The change admits drafts only when the PR's author is Nova's GitHub App. A person makes it, with Nave, as part of G2. Nova never edits workflow files; its protected paths deny .github/**.
sections.because: We widen the condition for exactly one author, so people's drafts behave as they do today.

code.text:
# fcp/.github/workflows/byte-review.yml: the change a PERSON makes (with Nave, under G2). Nova never edits workflow files.
# Today the pull_request path needs draft == false and the comment path skips bots, so a Nova draft never reaches Byte.
# Admit drafts only when the PR's author is Nova's GitHub App.
jobs:
  review:
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' &&
       github.event.action == 'created' &&
       github.event.issue.pull_request != null &&
       github.event.comment.user.type != 'Bot' &&
       (contains(github.event.comment.body, '@byte-review') ||
        contains(github.event.comment.body, '@byte-sniff'))) ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_review_comment' &&
       github.event.comment.user.type != 'Bot' &&
       github.event.comment.in_reply_to_id != null) ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
       (github.event.pull_request.draft == false ||
        github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'rhino-ai-agents[bot]') &&
       github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
       (github.event.action != 'review_requested' ||
        github.event.requested_team.slug == 'byte') &&
       (github.event.action != 'synchronize' ||
        contains(github.event.pull_request.requested_teams.*.slug, 'byte')))
    # bot login = the G0 app's slug + "[bot]" (confirm); the rest of the job is unchanged

notes.text: Who makes this change: a person, with Nave, under G2.
Path 1, unchanged: an @byte-review or @byte-sniff comment from a person.
Path 2, unchanged: a person replies to one of Byte's review comments.
Path 3: pull_request events. This is the path we change.
Before, only non-drafts passed. The new || lets a draft through when the next line is true.
The author is Nova's GitHub App. Confirm the login: the G0 app's slug plus [bot].
Only branches in fcp itself, never forks.
A review request counts only when the byte team was requested.
A new push re-runs Byte only while the byte team is still requested.

callout.text: G2-13 (lesson g2-5) describes this same change. Make it once, under G2-13, with Nave. G4-26 only checks that it is there.

sections.h: The ready gate: draft to ready only when clean
p: readyGate is a Temporal activity on the orchestrator. It collects blockers: anything that should stop people from being pinged. Any blocker keeps the PR a draft and pings nobody.

Required checks come from gh pr checks <n> --required through the broker. Each check has a bucket, GitHub CLI's group for its state: pass, fail, pending, skipping or cancel. Only pass and skipping are fine.
Sometimes main fails the same check. Then Nova links main's failing run as proof and flags it in the PR instead of looping. The sketch does not show that branch; agree with G3 how it is recorded.
sections.because: People's attention is the scarcest part of this loop, so they are pinged only for a PR with nothing left open.

notes.text: The gate's input from the shared package: qa_results, scope_judge, pr_judge, findings and reviewer_team.
Every GitHub call goes through the broker, scoped to one repo. The orchestrator holds no token either.
An important finding is done when it was fixed, answered with a reason, or handed to a person.
Only required checks. --json name,bucket returns each check's name and bucket.
A check that is not pass or skipping is a blocker, for example pending or fail.
Every QA check must have passed in the QA agent's own results (lesson g4-4). Nova cannot mark them.
A scope veto blocks until Nova reverted the change or explained it.
The PR judge must have nothing open.
Important findings from self-review and Byte that are not done yet.
Any blocker: stay a draft and return the list. Nobody is pinged.
Clean: mark the PR ready for review.
Request the team by area, for example RhinoHealth/frontend-guild for frontend/**.
The rest happens in ticketToPr: Nova state PR open, the ticket back to the requester, a Slack post.

callout.text: The G4-27 sketch has no branch for "main fails the same check". Without it, Nova keeps fixing a failure it did not cause. Add the branch in the PR: link main's failing run and flag it, as the text above says.

sections.h: After ready: people, one approval, reminders
p: When the gate passes, people hear about it once. The reviewer team is requested by area, as weekly-dependency-upgrades.yml does today: frontend-guild for frontend/**, backend-guild for cloud/** and client/**. The requester gets a Slack message, and the Jira ticket is assigned back to them.

Approval stays a GitHub wall. The fcp ruleset needs exactly one approval. G0's independent-approval check refuses the requester's approval, using the Requested-by line. The rhino-ai-agents app cannot merge and has no bypass.
After ready, review comments from people go into the same fix-or-answer loop as Byte's. If nobody reviews for 2 days, G3's reminders ping the team.

callout.text: Agents never merge. A Nova PR merges only after one approval from a person who is not the requester, with every required check green.

lab.title: Run the ready gate in your head (reading lab)

worked.do: Read G4-20 and list the body's headings in order, from top to bottom.
worked.see: What changes; Why; How it was checked; What was not checked, and why; Risk and rollback; Where to look first. Then the folded details, References and the Requested-by line.

worked.do: Predict readyGate's result. Required checks: Unit Tests pass, Build pending. QA-1 passed, QA-2 failed. Scope judge pass, PR judge ready. One important finding is answered.
worked.see: { ready: false, blockers: ["CI: Build is pending", "QA check QA-2 failed"] }. The PR stays a draft and nobody is pinged.

worked.do: Same evidence, but Build passes and QA-2 passes. Which two broker calls run?
worked.see: gh pr ready <n>, then gh pr edit <n> --add-reviewer <team>, for example RhinoHealth/frontend-guild.

worked.do: With the byte-review.yml change, Nova runs gh pr edit --add-reviewer RhinoHealth/byte on its draft. The event is pull_request, action review_requested, team byte, draft true, author rhino-ai-agents[bot]. Does the condition pass?
worked.see: Yes. draft == false is false, but the author line is true. The action is review_requested with slug byte, so the rest passes too.

worked.do: A person opens a draft and requests the byte team. Does the condition pass?
worked.see: No. The PR is a draft and the author is not Nova's app, so Byte waits until the PR is ready, as today.

worked.do: Find who reads the Requested-by line, and what it does with it.
worked.see: G0's independent-approval check. It puts that login in the requester set, so that person's approval never counts.

lab.faded: A Nova description overclaims. Its sentence: "Handles every edge case and adds full test coverage." The pack has only QA-1 and QA-2, no edge case. Write the PR judge's item as JSON: the sentence and the problem are given (problem: no_proof). The suggestion, a true rewrite, is left to you.
lab.alone: Write a PR body by hand for a made-up ticket RH-4321: "the datasets page spins forever on a 403". Use every pr-story heading, keep above the fold under 300 words, invent two QA checks with proof links, and end with Requested-by. Then read it as the PR judge and flag one sentence of your own.
lab.done: Given a GateEvidence, you can list the blockers. You can also say which line of the PR body each check reads.

quiz.q: CI is green and every QA check passed, but one important Byte finding is still in state open. What does readyGate do?

options.text: Marks the PR ready and lists the finding in the PR body
options.why: An open important finding is a blocker. People are pinged only when nothing important is open.

options.text: Keeps the PR a draft, returns the open finding as a blocker, and pings nobody
options.why: The open list is built from findings whose state is not fixed, answered or with_a_person.

options.text: Closes the PR and starts a new attempt
options.why: Nothing is closed. Nova fixes or answers the finding, and the gate runs again.

quiz.q: Who changes fcp's byte-review.yml so Byte reviews Nova's drafts?

options.text: Nova, in its first PR, because the change is small
options.why: Nova never edits workflow files; .github/** is a protected path.

options.text: The ready gate, at run time, through the broker
options.why: The gate only reads checks and marks PRs ready. Workflow files change by a reviewed PR.

options.text: A person, with Nave, as part of G2
options.why: Agents never change the checks or workflows they are judged by.

quiz.q: What does the PR judge get as input?

options.text: The description, the diff and the evidence pack, but never the transcript
options.why: It reads like a reviewer from another team: the page and the proof, not Nova's reasoning.

options.text: The transcript too, so it understands what Nova meant
options.why: Knowing the intent makes a judge kinder to unclear text. It must judge what is written.

options.text: Only the description, so it stays neutral
options.why: Without the diff and the evidence it cannot tell a true claim from an overclaim.

A PR GitHub marks as not ready for review; Nova keeps its PR a draft until the gate passes.
The activity that marks a draft ready only when CI, QA, both judges and all important findings are clean.
The GitHub CLI's group for a check's state: pass, fail, pending, skipping or cancel.
